page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-2 is an entry-level, compute-proportioned virtual machine within the E2 instance family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. It does not include any bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of cloud compute resources. In stress-ng testing, it achieves a single-core CPU score of 1105.98 and a multi-core score of 1452.89, both falling into the weak or poor categories. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with read-only large block transfers registering at 13.03 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.11 GB/sec. Geekbench evaluations return a single-core score of 906.0 and a multi-core score of 1073.0, reflecting limited processing capability for complex computational tasks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highcpu-2 offers an economical hardware profile for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but have minimal memory requirements. The tradeoff for its low cost is a significant performance ceiling, as evidenced by its poor database operations score of 570.03 and a static web serving throughput of 1.39 GB/sec. It is best suited for lightweight utility services, basic web serving, small-scale background workers, and low-demand microservices that do not require high memory capacity or rapid disk I/O.
